---
title: "Exp 1 & 2 Behavioral Statistical Analysis: GLMM (rejection rate) + LMM (logRT)"
subtitle: "Bates 5-step random-structure selection (Matuschek et al., 2017). RT analyses run in two strata: (i) main model on all valid trials with emotion x offer_type; (ii) unfair-only trials with emotion x reaction, parallel to HDDM modeling. Reporting upgraded to APA standard: 95% CI on all estimates, partial eta-squared for omnibus tests, odds ratios for GLMM, percent RT change for LMM."
author: "Project Research Team"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output: 
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
    code_folding: show
    theme: flatly
    fig_width: 10
    fig_height: 6

``` {r setup, include=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# 1. Global Configuration & Environment
# ==============================================================================
# Note: knitr defaults buffer chunk output until completion. For long-running
# chunks (large GLMM fits), we set R.options(progress = TRUE) and use
# flush.console() inside helpers (see flush_progress() below). When running
# interactively in RStudio (not via Knit), output is unbuffered automatically.
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  results = "markup"
)
options(scipen = 999, digits = 4)
set.seed(2024)

# Sum-to-zero contrasts: required for valid Type III ANOVA in the presence of
# interactions, and for interpretable zero-correlation random-effect parameterizations.
# Reference: Schad, Vasishth, Hohenstein, & Kliegl (2020) on contrast coding.
options(contrasts = c("contr.sum", "contr.poly"))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Global Settings & Analysis Targets (SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
experiment_version <- "E2"  # Options: "E1" or "E2"

# Behavioral analyses to run. Each is a separate model fit.
# - GLMM_rejection : reject_binary ~ emotion * offer_type, all valid trials
# - LMM_RT_main    : logRT ~ emotion * offer_type, all valid trials
#                    Note: reaction is NOT included as covariate. Reaction is a
#                    downstream outcome of emotion x offer_type, so conditioning on
#                    it would induce collider bias (Rohrer, 2018, AMPPS) and
#                    distort the total emotion-on-RT effect. RT differences
#                    between accept vs reject trials are addressed via the
#                    unfair-only stratum below.
# - LMM_RT_unfair  : logRT ~ emotion * reaction, unfair trials only (HDDM-parallel)
analyses_to_run <- c("GLMM_rejection", "LMM_RT_main", "LMM_RT_unfair")

# Behavioral data filtering thresholds.
rt_lower_ms <- 300
rt_upper_ms <- 3000

# Post-hoc gating: confirmatory simple-effect decomposition is triggered ONLY
# when the omnibus interaction p < 0.05. Effects with 0.05 <= p < 0.10 are
# computed but written to Supplementary/ rather than the main result tables.
# This separates confirmatory from exploratory inference cleanly:
#   - Confirmatory (p < 0.05): main tables, reported in manuscript Results.
#   - Exploratory_Marginal (0.05 <= p < 0.10): supplementary tables, reported
#     in supplementary materials only, never as confirmatory evidence.
confirmatory_alpha <- 0.05
marginal_threshold <- 0.10

if(!require("pacman")) install.packages("pacman")
pacman::p_load(
  here, readr, readxl, dplyr, tidyr, stringr, tibble, purrr,  # Data wrangling
  lme4, lmerTest, glmmTMB,                                     # Modeling
  pbkrtest,                                                    # Kenward-Roger backend for lmerTest
  car, parameters, performance,                                # Diagnostics
  buildmer,                                                    # LRT-based structure search (LMM + GLMM via buildglmmTMB)
  R.utils,                                                     # withTimeout for buildmer protection
  emmeans, effectsize,                                         # Marginal means, effect sizes
  sjPlot, sjmisc,                                              # tab_model, plot_model
  ggplot2, ggpubr, gridExtra,                                  # Publication visualization
  knitr, kableExtra,                                           # Markdown table rendering
  openxlsx                                                     # Legacy Excel export
)

# Inferential strategy: cascading method preference for LMM (Satterthwaite ->
# Kenward-Roger -> Wald); Wald-only for GLMM (Satterthwaite is mathematically
# undefined for non-Gaussian likelihoods because the approximation requires a
# residual variance term that does not exist in the binomial likelihood).
# 
# Empirical tests show Satterthwaite F-tests succeed in < 1 second on N > 20,000
# trials with complex random structures, provided lmerTest.limit and
# pbkrtest.limit are raised above the data size. Earlier pipeline versions 
# silently fell back to Wald due to default limits being too low; this is fixed.
# 
# Kenward-Roger is added as a middle fallback because it uses a different
# numerical implementation (pbkrtest::KRmodcomp) than Satterthwaite. When
# Satterthwaite hits Hessian inversion failure on certain random structures
# (e.g., (0 + offer_type | id) at the boundary), KR can still succeed.
# Empirical Type I error rates from Luke (2017) show KR is the most
# conservative of the three; it slightly under-powers vs Satterthwaite at
# small N but is essentially identical at large N.
# 
# Post-hoc contrasts via emmeans use asymptotic (z-test) df for computational
# stability on large datasets. At present DenDF magnitudes (DenDF >> 30),
# z-tests differ from Satterthwaite-based t-tests by less than 1% (Luke, 2017).
emmeans::emm_options(lmerTest.limit = 1e7, pbkrtest.limit = 1e7,
                     lmer.df = "asymptotic")
options(lmerTest.limit = 1e7)
options(pbkrtest.limit = 1e7)

# Output directory tree.
out_root    <- here("results", "Behavior", paste0(experiment_version, "_TwoStage_Bates"))
out_glmm    <- file.path(out_root, "GLMM_Rejection")
out_lmm_main   <- file.path(out_root, "LMM_RT_main")
out_lmm_unfair <- file.path(out_root, "LMM_RT_unfair")
out_tables  <- file.path(out_root, "Tables_Manuscript")
out_suppl   <- file.path(out_root, "Supplementary")
for (d in c(out_glmm, out_lmm_main, out_lmm_unfair, out_tables, out_suppl)) {
  if (!dir.exists(d)) dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE)
}

cat(sprintf("Behavioral pipeline initialized for Experiment: %s\nRoot: %s\nAnalyses: %s\nRT filter: %d-%d ms\n",
            experiment_version, out_root,
            paste(analyses_to_run, collapse=", "),
            rt_lower_ms, rt_upper_ms))

# Visual theme.
theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
          theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), legend.position = "top"))

colors_emo <- c('neu'="#8491B4",'aff'="#91D1C2",'dis'="#E64B35",'dom'="#F39B7F",'enj'="#3C5488")
labels_emo <- c('neu'='Neutral','aff'='Affiliative','dis'='Disgust','dom'='Dominance','enj'='Reward')
colors_off <- c('fair'="#2E86AB",'unfair'="#A23B72")
labels_off <- c('fair'='Fair', 'unfair'='Unfair')
colors_rxn <- c('accept'="#3C5488", 'reject'="#E64B35")
labels_rxn <- c('accept'='Accept', 'reject'='Reject')

# Optimizers and modeling engines.
# 
# DESIGN: GLMM and LMM use different engines but both follow Bates 5-step + 
# buildmer LRT simplification (Matuschek et al., 2017, alpha = 0.20).
# 
# LMM (Gaussian, lme4 + lmerTest):
#   - bobyqa optimizer; closed-form likelihood -> lme4::lmer.
#   - Step 3 simplification via buildmer::buildmer().
# 
# GLMM (binomial, glmmTMB):
#   - glmmTMB engine (Brooks et al., 2017): Template Model Builder backend
#     with autodiff, ~2-10x faster than lme4::glmer for binomial models.
#   - Step 3 simplification via buildmer::buildglmmTMB().
#   - emmeans, car::Anova, sjPlot::tab_model are all glmmTMB-compatible.
# 
# ENGINEERING: Both buildmer paths protected against deadlock via:
#   (a) lmerTest temporarily detached during buildmer (prevents Satterthwaite
#       Hessian inversion deadlock at large N);
#   (b) R.utils::withTimeout 1800-second hard limit;
#   (c) Fallback to ZCP model if buildmer times out or errors.
custom_control_lmer  <- lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa",
                                    optCtrl = list(maxfun = 200000),
                                    calc.derivs = FALSE)
custom_control_glmmTMB <- glmmTMB::glmmTMBControl(
  optimizer = optim,
  optArgs = list(method = "BFGS"),
  parallel = 1
)

# Null-coalescing helper for safe attribute fallback.
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Buildmer engineering helpers.
# 
# Two recurring failure modes for buildmer on large datasets:
#   (1) lmerTest, when loaded, intercepts ALL anova() calls and forces
#       Satterthwaite df computation. Inside buildmer's iterative LRT loop,
#       this triggers Hessian inversions for every candidate model. On certain
#       random structures (e.g., (0 + offer_type | id)) at large N (> 20K),
#       these Hessian inversions hang indefinitely, manifesting as CPU 0%
#       deadlock. SOLUTION: detach lmerTest before buildmer, reload after.
#   (2) Even without lmerTest, buildmer can occasionally hang on a single
#       optimization iteration. SOLUTION: wrap buildmer in withTimeout
#       (R.utils package); on timeout, fall back to ZCP model.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Safe lmerTest detach helper. Returns TRUE if lmerTest was attached and we
# detached it (caller should reload after buildmer). Returns FALSE if it
# wasn't attached.
detach_lmerTest_safely <- function() {
  if ("package:lmerTest" %in% search()) {
    detach("package:lmerTest", unload = FALSE, character.only = FALSE)
    return(TRUE)
  }
  FALSE
}

# Re-attach lmerTest (only if it was detached by us).
reattach_lmerTest_safely <- function(was_detached) {
  if (isTRUE(was_detached)) {
    suppressMessages(library(lmerTest))
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Wrap buildmer call in withTimeout; on timeout, return NULL so caller falls
# back to ZCP. timeout_sec defaults to 1200 (20 minutes).
run_buildmer_protected <- function(buildmer_fn, ..., timeout_sec = 1800) {
  # IMPORTANT: R.utils::withTimeout interrupts R-level loops but cannot interrupt
  # blocking C-level calls (e.g., the optimizer's inner loop). For deeply stuck
  # buildmer iterations, you may still need to manually interrupt R (Ctrl+C / 
  # ESC). Timeout offers protection against MOST stuck states (R loop hangs)
  # but is not 100% guaranteed.
  was_lmerTest <- detach_lmerTest_safely()
  on.exit(reattach_lmerTest_safely(was_lmerTest), add = TRUE)
  
  result <- tryCatch({
    R.utils::withTimeout({
      buildmer_fn(...)
    }, timeout = timeout_sec, onTimeout = "error")
  }, TimeoutException = function(ex) {
    progress_log(sprintf("[TIMEOUT] buildmer exceeded %d seconds; aborting.",
                         timeout_sec), indent = 2)
    NULL
  }, error = function(e) {
    if (grepl("reached.*time.*limit|timeout", conditionMessage(e), ignore.case = TRUE)) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[TIMEOUT] buildmer exceeded %d seconds; aborting.",
                           timeout_sec), indent = 2)
      NULL
    } else {
      progress_log(sprintf("[WARN] buildmer error: %s", conditionMessage(e)),
                   indent = 2)
      NULL
    }
  })
  
  result
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Progress reporting helpers (consistent with EEG pipeline v12).
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
flush_progress <- function() {
  flush.console()
  if (interactive()) Sys.sleep(0)
}

progress_log <- function(msg, indent = 0) {
  prefix <- strrep("  ", indent)
  cat(sprintf("%s%s\n", prefix, msg))
  flush_progress()
}

format_elapsed <- function(t_start) {
  secs <- as.numeric(Sys.time() - t_start, units = "secs")
  if (secs < 60) sprintf("%.1fs", secs)
  else if (secs < 3600) sprintf("%dm%02ds", floor(secs / 60), round(secs %% 60))
  else sprintf("%dh%02dm", floor(secs / 3600), floor((secs %% 3600) / 60))
}
```

``` {r apa-module}
# ==============================================================================
# 2. Helper Functions (consistent with v12 EEG pipeline).
# ==============================================================================

# Universal type conversion, missing-value handling, and column purging.
kill_scipen <- function(df) {
  df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.factor), as.character)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(across(everything(), function(vec) {
      if (is.numeric(vec)) {
        vec <- format(round(vec, 4), scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
      }
      vec <- ifelse(is.infinite(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(vec))), "Inf", vec)
      vec <- ifelse(is.na(vec) | vec == "NA", "-", as.character(vec))
      vec
    })) %>%
    dplyr::select(where(~ !all(. == "-")))
}

# APA significance star generator.
add_sig_stars <- function(p) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    is.na(p)  ~ "-",
    p < 0.001 ~ "***",
    p < 0.01  ~ "**",
    p < 0.05  ~ "*",
    p < 0.1   ~ ".",
    TRUE      ~ "ns"
  )
}

# Map sum-coding suffixes back to interpretable factor-level labels.
beautify_labels <- function(df) {
  dict <- c(
    "\\bemotion1\\b"    = "emotion[neu-grand]",
    "\\bemotion2\\b"    = "emotion[aff-grand]",
    "\\bemotion3\\b"    = "emotion[dis-grand]",
    "\\bemotion4\\b"    = "emotion[dom-grand]",
    "\\boffer_type1\\b" = "offer_type[fair-grand]",
    "\\breaction1\\b"   = "reaction[accept-grand]"
  )
  df %>% dplyr::mutate(across(where(is.character),
                              ~ stringr::str_replace_all(., dict)))
}

# Format ANOVA table to APA strings. Handles both F-tests (lmerTest::anova) and
# chi-square tests (car::Anova) seamlessly.
#
# For LMM F-tests: appends partial eta-squared with 95% CI from
# effectsize::eta_squared(). For GLMM Wald chi-square tests: partial
# eta-squared is not directly defined; effect size on the appropriate scale
# (odds ratio) is reported in the post-hoc contrasts table instead.
format_anova_apa <- function(anova_obj, model = NULL) {
  df_res <- as.data.frame(anova_obj) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("Effect")
  
  get_col <- function(col_name) {
    if (col_name %in% names(df_res)) df_res[[col_name]] else rep(NA, nrow(df_res))
  }
  
  df_res <- df_res %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      F_val  = get_col("F value"),
      NumDF  = get_col("NumDF"),
      DenDF  = get_col("DenDF"),
      Df_val = get_col("Df"),
      Chisq  = get_col("Chisq"),
      p_val  = dplyr::case_when(
        !is.na(get_col("Pr(>F)"))     ~ get_col("Pr(>F)"),
        !is.na(get_col("Pr(>Chisq)")) ~ get_col("Pr(>Chisq)"),
        TRUE ~ NA_real_
      ),
      Sig = add_sig_stars(p_val),
      p_str = dplyr::case_when(
        is.na(p_val)  ~ "-",
        p_val < .001  ~ "< .001",
        TRUE          ~ paste0("= ", format(round(p_val, 3), scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE))
      ),
      APA_Report = dplyr::case_when(
        !is.na(F_val) & !is.na(NumDF) & !is.na(DenDF) ~
          sprintf("F(%s, %.2f) = %.2f, p %s", NumDF, DenDF, F_val, p_str),
        !is.na(F_val) & !is.na(NumDF) ~
          sprintf("F(%s) = %.2f, p %s", NumDF, F_val, p_str),
        !is.na(Chisq) & !is.na(Df_val) ~
          sprintf("\u03C7\u00B2(%s) = %.2f, p %s", Df_val, Chisq, p_str),
        TRUE ~ "[stat unrecognized]"
      )
    )
  
  # Partial eta-squared with 95% CI: only for LMM F-tests (Gaussian).
  # For GLMM chi-square, eta-squared is not directly defined; we leave the
  # column NA and rely on odds ratios in the post-hoc table for effect size.
  has_F <- "F value" %in% names(as.data.frame(anova_obj))
  
  eta2_df <- NULL
  if (has_F) {
    eta2_df <- tryCatch({
      es <- effectsize::eta_squared(anova_obj, partial = TRUE, ci = 0.95,
                                    alternative = "two.sided",
                                    verbose = FALSE)
      data.frame(
        Effect = as.character(es$Parameter),
        eta2_partial = es$Eta2_partial,
        eta2_CI_low  = es$CI_low,
        eta2_CI_high = es$CI_high,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    }, error = function(e) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[ANOVA] eta-squared computation failed: %s",
                           conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
      NULL
    })
  }
  
  if (!is.null(eta2_df)) {
    df_res <- df_res %>%
      dplyr::left_join(eta2_df, by = "Effect") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        eta2_str = dplyr::case_when(
          is.na(eta2_partial) ~ "-",
          TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]",
                         eta2_partial, eta2_CI_low, eta2_CI_high)
        )
      )
  } else {
    df_res$eta2_str <- "-"
  }
  
  df_res <- df_res %>%
    dplyr::select(Effect, APA_Report, eta2_partial_95CI = eta2_str, Sig, p_val)
  beautify_labels(df_res)
}

# Format post-hoc emmeans output. Switches to z-statistic notation when df is
# infinite (asymptotic / GLMM cases).
#
# Reporting upgrades over v1:
# - 95% CI on the estimate (always).
# - Odds ratio with 95% CI (when input is on logit scale, i.e. GLMM contrasts).
# - Percent RT change (when scale_hint == "logRT", i.e. LMM logRT contrasts).
#
# scale_hint argument:
#   "auto"   - auto-detect from estimate column name (default; matches v1 API)
#   "logit"  - GLMM logit-scale estimates; compute odds ratios
#   "logRT"  - LMM log-RT estimates; compute percent RT change
#   "raw"    - report estimate as-is, no transformation
format_posthoc_apa <- function(emm_df, scale_hint = "auto") {
  df_clean <- as.data.frame(emm_df)
  
  est_col <- intersect(names(df_clean),
                       c("estimate", "emmean", "response", "odds.ratio"))
  if (length(est_col) == 0) {
    trend_col <- grep("\\.trend$", names(df_clean), value = TRUE)
    est_col <- if (length(trend_col) > 0) trend_col[1] else names(df_clean)[2]
  } else {
    est_col <- est_col[1]
  }
  
  # Auto-detect scale.
  if (scale_hint == "auto") {
    if (est_col == "odds.ratio") {
      scale_hint <- "odds_ratio_input"
    } else {
      scale_hint <- "raw"
    }
  }
  
  # Confidence intervals: emmeans output should already include lower.CL /
  # upper.CL when summary(infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) was used. If absent, compute
  # from estimate +/- 1.96 * SE (Wald-based, asymptotic).
  has_ci <- all(c("lower.CL", "upper.CL") %in% names(df_clean))
  if (!has_ci) {
    df_clean$lower.CL <- df_clean[[est_col]] - 1.96 * df_clean$SE
    df_clean$upper.CL <- df_clean[[est_col]] + 1.96 * df_clean$SE
  }
  
  df_clean <- df_clean %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Sig = add_sig_stars(p.value),
      p_str = dplyr::case_when(
        p.value < .001 ~ "< .001",
        TRUE ~ paste0("= ", format(round(p.value, 3), scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE))
      ),
      CI_str = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", lower.CL, upper.CL)
    )
  
  if ("t.ratio" %in% names(df_clean)) {
    df_clean <- df_clean %>% dplyr::mutate(
      Stats_String = ifelse(
        is.infinite(df),
        sprintf("b = %.2f (SE = %.2f), 95%% CI %s, z = %.2f, p %s",
                .data[[est_col]], SE, CI_str, t.ratio, p_str),
        sprintf("b = %.2f (SE = %.2f), 95%% CI %s, t(%.2f) = %.2f, p %s",
                .data[[est_col]], SE, CI_str, df, t.ratio, p_str)
      )
    )
  } else if ("z.ratio" %in% names(df_clean)) {
    df_clean <- df_clean %>% dplyr::mutate(
      Stats_String = sprintf("b = %.2f (SE = %.2f), 95%% CI %s, z = %.2f, p %s",
                             .data[[est_col]], SE, CI_str, z.ratio, p_str)
    )
  } else {
    df_clean <- df_clean %>% dplyr::mutate(
      Stats_String = sprintf("b = %.2f (SE = %.2f), 95%% CI %s, p %s",
                             .data[[est_col]], SE, CI_str, p_str)
    )
  }
  
  # Scale-specific effect size additions.
  if (scale_hint == "logit") {
    # GLMM logit-scale contrasts: append OR with 95% CI.
    # Adaptive precision: standard %.2f formatting collapses extreme ORs
    # (e.g. OR = 0.0019 with strong fair/unfair effect rounds to "0.00",
    # erasing the actual effect magnitude). When |log10(OR)| > 1.5 (i.e.
    # OR < ~0.03 or OR > ~30), switch to %.4f precision so readers can see
    # the effect.
    df_clean <- df_clean %>% dplyr::mutate(
      OR          = exp(.data[[est_col]]),
      OR_CI_low   = exp(lower.CL),
      OR_CI_high  = exp(upper.CL),
      OR_String   = mapply(function(or_val, lo, hi) {
        magnitude <- max(abs(log10(or_val)), abs(log10(lo)), abs(log10(hi)),
                         na.rm = TRUE)
        if (is.finite(magnitude) && magnitude > 1.5) {
          sprintf("OR = %.4f, 95%% CI [%.4f, %.4f]", or_val, lo, hi)
        } else {
          sprintf("OR = %.2f, 95%% CI [%.2f, %.2f]", or_val, lo, hi)
        }
      }, OR, OR_CI_low, OR_CI_high)
    )
  } else if (scale_hint == "logRT") {
    # LMM log-RT contrasts: append percent RT change.
    # b on log scale -> percent change in raw RT = (exp(b) - 1) * 100
    df_clean <- df_clean %>% dplyr::mutate(
      PctChange       = (exp(.data[[est_col]]) - 1) * 100,
      PctChange_low   = (exp(lower.CL) - 1) * 100,
      PctChange_high  = (exp(upper.CL) - 1) * 100,
      PctChange_String = sprintf("RT change = %+.2f%%, 95%% CI [%+.2f%%, %+.2f%%]",
                                  PctChange, PctChange_low, PctChange_high)
    )
  } else if (scale_hint == "odds_ratio_input") {
    # emmeans was called with type = "response" on a logit model;
    # the est_col is already odds.ratio. CI columns already exist.
    df_clean <- df_clean %>% dplyr::mutate(
      OR_String = sprintf("OR = %.2f, 95%% CI %s", .data[[est_col]], CI_str)
    )
  }
  
  df_clean <- df_clean %>%
    dplyr::select(-p_str) %>%
    dplyr::relocate(Sig, .after = Stats_String)
  beautify_labels(df_clean)
}

# Extract fixed-effect coefficients with safe fallback.
format_coefs <- function(model) {
  tryCatch({
    coefs <- as.data.frame(parameters::parameters(model, effects = "fixed"))
    coefs %>% beautify_labels() %>% kill_scipen()
  }, error = function(e) {
    as.data.frame(summary(model)$coefficients) %>%
      tibble::rownames_to_column("Predictor") %>%
      beautify_labels() %>% kill_scipen()
  })
}

# Cell-level descriptive statistics for the manuscript Table 1.
#
# Outputs per (emotion x offer_type) cell:
#   N_subjects, N_trials, rejection_rate, mean_RT, SD_RT, median_RT, IQR_RT
# and overall participant counts. Designed for direct manuscript inclusion.
#
# stratify_var allows splitting (e.g., by reaction for unfair-only analysis).
format_descriptives_table <- function(df, group_vars = c("emotion", "offer_type")) {
  # Coerce to character to ensure stable group order.
  group_vars <- intersect(group_vars, names(df))
  if (length(group_vars) == 0) {
    return(data.frame(Note = "No grouping variables found in data."))
  }
  
  desc <- df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(across(all_of(group_vars))) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      N_subjects     = dplyr::n_distinct(participant_id),
      N_trials       = dplyr::n(),
      Rejection_rate = mean(reject_binary, na.rm = TRUE),
      Mean_RT_ms     = mean(RT, na.rm = TRUE),
      SD_RT_ms       = sd(RT, na.rm = TRUE),
      Median_RT_ms   = median(RT, na.rm = TRUE),
      IQR_RT_ms      = IQR(RT, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Rejection_rate = sprintf("%.3f", Rejection_rate),
      Mean_RT_ms     = sprintf("%.0f", Mean_RT_ms),
      SD_RT_ms       = sprintf("%.0f", SD_RT_ms),
      Median_RT_ms   = sprintf("%.0f", Median_RT_ms),
      IQR_RT_ms      = sprintf("%.0f", IQR_RT_ms)
    )
  
  beautify_labels(desc)
}
```

``` {r prep-functions}
# ==============================================================================
# 3. Data Loading & Cleaning
# ==============================================================================

standardize_id <- function(ids) {
  sprintf("Vp%04d", as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(ids, "\\d+")))
}

# Behavioral data loader.
#
# Filters and exclusions:
# 1. Offers_Other in {5, 6, 8, 9}: standard fair/unfair offer pairs
# 2. reaction != 0: excludes timeout / no-response trials (~92 in E2 data)
# 3. RT in [rt_lower_ms, rt_upper_ms]: excludes premature responses and
#    response-window-exceeding trials
#
# Generated columns:
# - offer_type: factor("fair", "unfair") from Offers_Other
# - emotion:    factor with levels c("neu","aff","dis","dom","enj")
# - reaction:   factor("accept", "reject") -- recoded from numeric (1=accept, 2=reject)
# - reject_binary: numeric 0/1 for GLMM outcome (reject=1)
# - logRT:      log-transformed RT for LMM (variance-stabilizing for skewed RT)
load_and_prep_behavior <- function(path_trials) {
  if (!file.exists(path_trials)) {
    stop(sprintf("Behavioral data file missing: %s", path_trials))
  }
  
  df <- readr::read_csv(path_trials, show_col_types = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("[Load] Raw N = %d trials, %d subjects\n",
              nrow(df), dplyr::n_distinct(df$participant_id)))
  
  required_cols <- c("participant_id", "Offers_Other", "emotion", "reaction", "RT", "index")
  missing_cols <- setdiff(required_cols, names(df))
  if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
    stop(sprintf("Required columns missing: %s", paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  
  df$participant_id <- standardize_id(df$participant_id)
  
  # Apply filters in sequence with logging.
  n_orig <- nrow(df)
  
  # Filter 1: standard fair/unfair offers only.
  df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(Offers_Other %in% c(5, 6, 8, 9))
  cat(sprintf("[Filter] Offers_Other in {5,6,8,9}: %d -> %d trials (%.1f%% kept)\n",
              n_orig, nrow(df), 100 * nrow(df) / n_orig))
  
  # Filter 2: exclude reaction = 0 (timeout / missing).
  n_pre <- nrow(df)
  df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(reaction != 0)
  cat(sprintf("[Filter] reaction != 0 (timeout): %d -> %d trials (%d removed)\n",
              n_pre, nrow(df), n_pre - nrow(df)))
  
  # Filter 3: RT range.
  n_pre <- nrow(df)
  df <- df %>% dplyr::filter(RT >= rt_lower_ms, RT <= rt_upper_ms)
  cat(sprintf("[Filter] RT in [%d, %d] ms: %d -> %d trials (%d removed)\n",
              rt_lower_ms, rt_upper_ms, n_pre, nrow(df), n_pre - nrow(df)))
  
  # Construct factors and outcome variables.
  df <- df %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      offer_type = factor(
        dplyr::case_when(
          Offers_Other %in% c(5, 6) ~ "fair",
          Offers_Other %in% c(8, 9) ~ "unfair"
        ),
        levels = c("fair", "unfair")
      ),
      emotion = factor(emotion, levels = c("neu", "aff", "dis", "dom", "enj")),
      # Recode reaction: 1 -> accept, 2 -> reject (verified from data inspection)
      reaction = factor(
        dplyr::case_when(
          reaction == 1 ~ "accept",
          reaction == 2 ~ "reject"
        ),
        levels = c("accept", "reject")
      ),
      # Binary outcome for GLMM (reject = 1, accept = 0 as user specified)
      reject_binary = ifelse(reaction == "reject", 1, 0),
      # Log-RT for LMM. Avoids assumption of Gaussian RT and stabilizes variance
      # for the typical RT skew distribution (cf. Lo & Andrews, 2015).
      logRT = log(RT)
    )
  
  cat(sprintf("[Final] N = %d trials, %d subjects after all filters\n",
              nrow(df), dplyr::n_distinct(df$participant_id)))
  
  # Sanity check: print accept/reject distribution by offer_type.
  cat("\n[Distribution] reaction x offer_type:\n")
  print(table(df$reaction, df$offer_type))
  
  df
}

check_uniqueness <- function(df, context_name) {
  if (nrow(df) != dplyr::n_distinct(dplyr::select(df, participant_id, index))) {
    stop(sprintf("CRITICAL: duplicate (participant_id, index) keys in %s.", context_name))
  }
}
```
