``` {r bates-engine}
# ==============================================================================
# 4. Stage 1 Engine: Bates 5-step random-structure selection
#    Adapted from EEG v12 pipeline. Behavioral version omits Alday baseline
#    framework (no pre-stimulus baseline in behavioral data).
# ==============================================================================
#
# DIFFERENCES FROM EEG PIPELINE:
# (1) No Baseline_c covariate -- behavioral RT/decision has no pre-stimulus baseline;
# (2) GLMM (binomial) and LMM (Gaussian) paths share random-structure selection
#     logic but differ in fitting function (glmer vs lmer);
# (3) Forced-include set: emotion + offer_type + emotion:offer_type + (1|id),
#     same theoretical core as EEG. The optional additional fixed term varies
#     by analysis (e.g., 'reaction' for LMM_RT_unfair, no extra for GLMM/LMM_RT_main).
#
# RANDOM-EFFECT STRUCTURE (Bates 2015 / Matuschek 2017):
#   Step 1: Maximal model (1 + emotion + offer_type | participant_id)
#           Interaction random slope omitted by design (typically unidentifiable
#           with N_subjects ~30 in single-trial data).
#   Step 2: Zero-correlation-parameter (ZCP) model
#   Step 3: LRT-based backward elimination (alpha = 0.20, Matuschek et al. 2017)
#   Step 4: Re-test correlation parameters on surviving slopes
#   Step 5: rePCA dimensionality diagnostic
# ==============================================================================

# Helper: parse a fitted model's formula to identify which random slopes
# survived Step 3.
extract_surviving_slopes <- function(model) {
  re_terms <- lme4::findbars(formula(model))
  surviving <- character(0)
  for (term in re_terms) {
    rhs <- deparse(term[[2]])
    rhs <- gsub("^\\s*0\\s*\\+\\s*", "", rhs)
    rhs <- gsub("^\\s*1\\s*\\+\\s*", "", rhs)
    rhs <- gsub("^\\s*1\\s*$",       "", rhs)
    rhs <- trimws(rhs)
    if (rhs == "" || rhs == "1") next
    parts <- trimws(strsplit(rhs, "\\+")[[1]])
    surviving <- c(surviving, parts)
  }
  unique(surviving)
}

# Helper: rePCA dimensionality summary as tidy data frame.
extract_repca_summary <- function(model, group_name = "participant_id") {
  empty_df <- data.frame(component = NA_integer_, sd = NA_real_,
                         proportion_variance = NA_real_,
                         cumulative_variance = NA_real_)
  
  if (inherits(model, "merMod")) {
    # lme4 path: built-in rePCA function.
    pca_obj <- tryCatch(lme4::rePCA(model), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(pca_obj) || !group_name %in% names(pca_obj)) return(empty_df)
    imp <- summary(pca_obj[[group_name]])$importance
    return(data.frame(
      component = seq_len(ncol(imp)),
      sd = imp["Standard deviation", ],
      proportion_variance = imp["Proportion of Variance", ],
      cumulative_variance = imp["Cumulative Proportion", ]
    ))
  }
  
  if (inherits(model, "glmmTMB")) {
    # glmmTMB path: extract VarCorr -> compute SVD manually on combined cov matrix.
    # rePCA is principal-components analysis on the full random-effects covariance,
    # so we replicate this directly: combine all per-term covariances into a
    # block-diagonal matrix, compute SVD, return importance summary.
    vc_list <- VarCorr(model)$cond
    if (is.null(vc_list)) return(empty_df)
    
    # Find all terms grouped by the requested group.
    relevant <- vc_list[names(vc_list) == group_name |
                        grepl(paste0("^", group_name), names(vc_list))]
    if (length(relevant) == 0) {
      relevant <- vc_list  # Fallback: use all if name match fails.
    }
    
    # Combine covariance matrices into block-diagonal.
    cov_mats <- lapply(relevant, function(x) as.matrix(x))
    total_dim <- sum(sapply(cov_mats, function(x) nrow(x)))
    big_cov <- matrix(0, total_dim, total_dim)
    pos <- 0
    for (m in cov_mats) {
      d <- nrow(m)
      big_cov[(pos + 1):(pos + d), (pos + 1):(pos + d)] <- m
      pos <- pos + d
    }
    
    # SVD-based importance: same logic as lme4::rePCA.
    sv <- tryCatch(svd(big_cov)$d, error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(sv) || length(sv) == 0) return(empty_df)
    
    sv <- pmax(sv, 0)  # numerical zero clamp
    sds <- sqrt(sv)
    if (sum(sv) <= 0) return(empty_df)
    prop <- sv / sum(sv)
    cum_prop <- cumsum(prop)
    
    return(data.frame(
      component = seq_along(sds),
      sd = sds,
      proportion_variance = prop,
      cumulative_variance = cum_prop
    ))
  }
  
  empty_df
}

count_effective_dims <- function(repca_df, threshold = 0.999) {
  if (all(is.na(repca_df$cumulative_variance))) return(NA_integer_)
  hit <- which(repca_df$cumulative_variance >= threshold)
  if (length(hit) == 0) nrow(repca_df) else hit[1]
}

# Step 4 helper: enumerate candidate correlated structures.
# Note: model_family argument selects between lmer and glmer for fitting.
add_correlations_step4 <- function(model_zcp_reduced, fixed_str, data,
                                   model_family = "gaussian", alpha_lrt = 0.20) {
  if (!inherits(model_zcp_reduced, c("merMod", "glmmTMB"))) {
    progress_log("[Step 4] Reduced model is not a mixed model; skipping correlation tests.",
                 indent = 1)
    return(model_zcp_reduced)
  }
  
  surviving <- extract_surviving_slopes(model_zcp_reduced)
  
  if (length(surviving) == 0) {
    progress_log("[Step 4] Reduced model has only random intercept; no correlations to test.",
                 indent = 1)
    return(model_zcp_reduced)
  }
  
  candidates <- list()
  candidates[["ZCP_reference"]] <- formula(model_zcp_reduced)
  
  all_str <- paste(surviving, collapse = " + ")
  candidates[["All_correlated"]] <- as.formula(
    paste(fixed_str, "+ (1 +", all_str, "| participant_id)")
  )
  
  if (length(surviving) > 1) {
    for (i in seq_along(surviving)) {
      others <- setdiff(surviving, surviving[i])
      if (length(others) > 0) {
        others_terms <- paste(
          sprintf("(0 + %s | participant_id)", others),
          collapse = " + "
        )
        cand_str <- paste(fixed_str,
                          sprintf("+ (1 + %s | participant_id)", surviving[i]),
                          "+", others_terms)
      } else {
        cand_str <- paste(fixed_str,
                          sprintf("+ (1 + %s | participant_id)", surviving[i]))
      }
      candidates[[paste0("Int_with_", surviving[i])]] <- as.formula(cand_str)
    }
  }
  
  total_cands <- length(candidates)
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4] Fitting %d candidate correlated structures (%s)...",
                       total_cands, model_family), indent = 1)
  
  fits <- list()
  cand_idx <- 0
  for (nm in names(candidates)) {
    cand_idx <- cand_idx + 1
    progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] Trying '%s'...",
                         cand_idx, total_cands, nm), indent = 2)
    t_cand <- Sys.time()
    
    fit <- tryCatch({
      if (model_family == "binomial") {
        # glmmTMB engine for GLMM. Singular-fit detection differs from lme4:
        # glmmTMB uses optimizer convergence + variance > 0 check.
        glmmTMB::glmmTMB(candidates[[nm]], data = data,
                         family = binomial(link = "logit"),
                         control = custom_control_glmmTMB,
                         REML = FALSE)
      } else {
        lme4::lmer(candidates[[nm]], data = data, REML = FALSE,
                   control = custom_control_lmer)
      }
    }, error = function(e) NULL)
    
    # Convergence + singularity check. For glmmTMB, we use is_singular_glmmTMB
    # helper (defined below); for lme4 we use lme4::isSingular.
    is_singular_check <- function(m) {
      if (inherits(m, "glmmTMB")) {
        # glmmTMB doesn't have isSingular; check if any random variance is
        # at boundary (effectively zero).
        vc <- VarCorr(m)$cond
        if (is.null(vc)) return(FALSE)
        vars <- unlist(lapply(vc, function(x) diag(as.matrix(x))))
        any(vars < 1e-6)
      } else {
        lme4::isSingular(m, tol = 1e-4)
      }
    }
    
    if (!is.null(fit) && !is_singular_check(fit)) {
      fits[[nm]] <- fit
      progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] '%s' converged (%s).",
                           cand_idx, total_cands, nm, format_elapsed(t_cand)),
                   indent = 3)
    } else if (!is.null(fit)) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] '%s' singular; excluded (%s).",
                           cand_idx, total_cands, nm, format_elapsed(t_cand)),
                   indent = 3)
    } else {
      progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4 %d/%d] '%s' failed to converge (%s).",
                           cand_idx, total_cands, nm, format_elapsed(t_cand)),
                   indent = 3)
    }
  }
  
  # All-singular fallback: degrade to random-intercept-only.
  if (length(fits) == 0) {
    progress_log("[Step 4] All candidates singular; data does not support random slopes.",
                 indent = 1)
    progress_log("[Step 4] Refitting with random-intercept-only structure.", indent = 2)
    
    fixed_only_part <- nobars(formula(model_zcp_reduced))
    f_min <- as.formula(paste(deparse(fixed_only_part), "+ (1 | participant_id)"))
    
    m_min <- if (model_family == "binomial") {
      glmmTMB::glmmTMB(f_min, data = data,
                       family = binomial(link = "logit"),
                       control = custom_control_glmmTMB,
                       REML = FALSE)
    } else {
      lme4::lmer(f_min, data = data, REML = TRUE,
                 control = custom_control_lmer)
    }
    
    attr(m_min, "step4_selected") <- "RandomIntercept_only"
    return(m_min)
  }
  
  if (length(fits) == 1) {
    progress_log("[Step 4] Only ZCP candidate viable; correlations not added.", indent = 1)
    if (model_family == "binomial") {
      return(model_zcp_reduced)
    } else {
      return(update(model_zcp_reduced, REML = TRUE))
    }
  }
  
  # Establish a working reference model for LRT comparisons. ZCP_reference is the
  # preferred reference point because all other candidates are nested within
  # it. If it failed to converge but other candidates succeeded, fall back to
  # the simplest converged candidate as the new reference (lowest AIC) and select between the
  # remaining candidates by AIC alone (no nested LRT possible).
  reference_fit <- fits[["ZCP_reference"]]
  lrt_table <- data.frame(model = character(), df_diff = integer(),
                          chisq = numeric(), p_value = numeric(),
                          AIC = numeric(), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  
  if (is.null(reference_fit)) {
    # ZCP_reference was singular but at least one alternative converged.
    # Select the candidate with lowest AIC; report the situation transparently.
    progress_log("[Step 4] ZCP_reference singular; selecting best converged candidate by AIC.",
                 indent = 1)
    aics <- sapply(fits, AIC)
    best_name <- names(fits)[which.min(aics)]
    best_fit  <- fits[[best_name]]
    
    # Populate lrt_table with AIC-only entries (no nested LRT performed because
    # the candidates are not nested in a way that supports clean LRT here).
    for (nm in names(fits)) {
      lrt_table <- rbind(lrt_table, data.frame(
        model = nm,
        df_diff = NA_integer_,
        chisq = NA_real_,
        p_value = NA_real_,
        AIC = aics[nm],
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      ))
    }
  } else {
    # Standard path: ZCP_reference available, perform nested LRTs against it.
    best_name <- "ZCP_reference"
    best_fit  <- reference_fit
    
    for (nm in setdiff(names(fits), "ZCP_reference")) {
      cand <- fits[[nm]]
      lrt <- tryCatch(anova(reference_fit, cand), error = function(e) NULL)
      if (is.null(lrt) || nrow(lrt) < 2) next
      
      p_val <- lrt$"Pr(>Chisq)"[2]
      if (is.na(p_val)) next
      
      lrt_table <- rbind(lrt_table, data.frame(
        model = nm,
        df_diff = lrt$Df[2],
        chisq = lrt$Chisq[2],
        p_value = p_val,
        AIC = AIC(cand),
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      ))
      
      if (p_val < alpha_lrt && AIC(cand) < AIC(best_fit)) {
        best_name <- nm
        best_fit  <- cand
      }
    }
  }
  
  attr(best_fit, "step4_lrt_table") <- lrt_table
  attr(best_fit, "step4_selected") <- best_name
  
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4] Selected: %s (alpha_LRT = %.2f).",
                       best_name, alpha_lrt), indent = 1)
  
  if (model_family == "binomial") {
    best_fit
  } else {
    update(best_fit, REML = TRUE)
  }
}

# ==============================================================================
# Main Bates 5-step engine. Branches on model_family.
# Inputs:
#   data:           clean trial-level data frame
#   outcome_var:    name of dependent variable (e.g., "reject_binary", "logRT")
#   fixed_terms:    string with right-hand side of fixed effects (without intercept)
#                   e.g., "(emotion + offer_type)^2" or "emotion * offer_type + reaction"
#   include_terms: character vector of fixed effects to force-keep in Step 3
#                   (theoretical core terms protected from LRT elimination)
#   model_family:   "gaussian" (LMM) or "binomial" (GLMM)
# ==============================================================================
fit_stage1_bates <- function(data, outcome_var, fixed_terms, include_terms,
                             model_family = "gaussian") {
  
  fixed_str <- sprintf("%s ~ %s", outcome_var, fixed_terms)
  
  fixed_include_str <- paste(include_terms, "+ (1 | participant_id)")
  fixed_include <- as.formula(sprintf("~ %s", fixed_include_str))
  
  diag_log <- list(
    outcome = outcome_var,
    family = model_family,
    n_obs = nrow(data),
    n_subjects = dplyr::n_distinct(data$participant_id),
    step1_status = NA_character_,
    step1_pca = NULL,
    step2_status = NA_character_,
    step3_final_formula = NA_character_,
    step4_status = NA_character_,
    step5_pca = NULL
  )
  
  # Determine random-slope variables based on outcome and design.
  # Behavioral analyses always use within-subject factors emotion and offer_type
  # as candidate random slopes (interaction omitted by design per Bates 2015).
  random_max_vars <- c("emotion", "offer_type")
  random_max_str <- paste("(1 +", paste(random_max_vars, collapse = " + "),
                          "| participant_id)")
  
  # Determine fitting function based on family.
  # GLMM: glmmTMB (TMB-based, faster + more stable on binomial than lme4::glmer)
  # LMM:  lme4::lmer (Gaussian, classic Bates 5-step compatible)
  fit_func <- function(formula, data, REML_flag = FALSE) {
    if (model_family == "binomial") {
      glmmTMB::glmmTMB(formula, data = data,
                       family = binomial(link = "logit"),
                       control = custom_control_glmmTMB,
                       REML = REML_flag)
    } else {
      lme4::lmer(formula, data = data, REML = REML_flag,
                 control = custom_control_lmer)
    }
  }
  
  # Singularity check that handles both engines.
  is_singular_check <- function(m) {
    if (inherits(m, "glmmTMB")) {
      vc <- VarCorr(m)$cond
      if (is.null(vc)) return(FALSE)
      vars <- unlist(lapply(vc, function(x) diag(as.matrix(x))))
      any(vars < 1e-6)
    } else {
      lme4::isSingular(m, tol = 1e-4)
    }
  }
  
  # ---- STEP 1: Barr-style maximal model ----
  progress_log(sprintf("[%s | %s] Stage 1: Bates 5-step random-structure selection",
                       outcome_var, model_family))
  progress_log(sprintf("Data: N = %d trials, %d subjects.",
                       nrow(data), dplyr::n_distinct(data$participant_id)),
               indent = 1)
  progress_log(sprintf("Fixed terms: %s", fixed_terms), indent = 1)
  progress_log(sprintf("Forced include: %s",
                       paste(include_terms, collapse = ", ")), indent = 1)
  
  f_max <- as.formula(paste(fixed_str, "+", random_max_str))
  
  progress_log("[Step 1] Fitting design-justified maximal model with correlations...",
               indent = 1)
  t_step1 <- Sys.time()
  m_max <- tryCatch(
    fit_func(f_max, data, REML_flag = FALSE),
    error = function(e) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[ERROR] Maximal fit failed: %s", conditionMessage(e)),
                   indent = 2)
      NULL
    }
  )
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 1] elapsed: %s", format_elapsed(t_step1)),
               indent = 2)
  
  if (!is.null(m_max)) {
    is_sing <- is_singular_check(m_max)
    diag_log$step1_status <- if (is_sing) "converged_singular" else "converged_clean"
    diag_log$step1_pca <- extract_repca_summary(m_max)
    progress_log(sprintf("[Step 1] Status: %s. Effective dims = %d / %d.",
                         diag_log$step1_status,
                         count_effective_dims(diag_log$step1_pca),
                         nrow(diag_log$step1_pca)),
                 indent = 2)
  } else {
    diag_log$step1_status <- "failed_to_converge"
  }
  
  # ---- STEP 2: ZCP model ----
  progress_log("[Step 2] Fitting zero-correlation-parameter model...", indent = 1)
  t_step2 <- Sys.time()
  
  random_zcp <- paste("(1 | participant_id)",
                      sprintf("(0 + %s | participant_id)", random_max_vars[1]),
                      sprintf("(0 + %s | participant_id)", random_max_vars[2]),
                      sep = " + ")
  f_zcp <- as.formula(paste(fixed_str, "+", random_zcp))
  
  m_zcp <- tryCatch(fit_func(f_zcp, data, REML_flag = FALSE),
                    error = function(e) NULL)
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 2] elapsed: %s", format_elapsed(t_step2)), indent = 2)
  
  if (is.null(m_zcp)) {
    progress_log("[Step 2] [ERROR] ZCP fit failed; falling back to random-intercept-only.",
                 indent = 2)
    diag_log$step2_status <- "failed"
    f_minimal <- as.formula(paste(fixed_str, "+ (1 | participant_id)"))
    m_zcp <- fit_func(f_minimal, data, REML_flag = FALSE)
  } else {
    is_sing_zcp <- is_singular_check(m_zcp)
    diag_log$step2_status <- if (is_sing_zcp) "converged_singular" else "converged_clean"
    progress_log(sprintf("[Step 2] Status: %s.", diag_log$step2_status), indent = 2)
  }
  
  # ---- STEP 3: buildmer LRT-based random-structure simplification ----
  # 
  # Both GLMM and LMM paths use buildmer's stepwise LRT elimination 
  # (Matuschek et al., 2017, alpha = 0.20). The interface differs by family:
  #   GLMM (binomial) -> buildmer::buildglmmTMB() with glmmTMB engine
  #   LMM  (gaussian) -> buildmer::buildmer() with lme4 engine
  # 
  # ENGINEERING PROTECTIONS (run_buildmer_protected helper):
  #   (1) lmerTest is detached before buildmer call to prevent Satterthwaite
  #       Hessian inversions inside buildmer's iterative LRT loop, which can
  #       cause CPU 0% deadlock on large datasets with complex random structures.
  #   (2) R.utils::withTimeout (1200s default) prevents indefinite hangs.
  #   (3) On timeout or error, falls back to ZCP model.
  
  progress_log("[Step 3] LRT-based backward elimination (buildmer, alpha = 0.20)...",
               indent = 1)
  progress_log(paste("This step iteratively tests model terms via LRT and may fit",
                     "many candidate models. With large N or complex random",
                     "structures, expect several minutes."),
               indent = 2)
  t_step3 <- Sys.time()
  
  if (model_family == "binomial") {
    # GLMM path via buildglmmTMB.
    progress_log("[Step 3] Engine: buildglmmTMB (glmmTMB-based LRT elimination).",
                 indent = 2)
    bm_ctrl <- buildmer::buildmerControl(
      include = fixed_include,
      direction = c("order", "backward"),
      crit = "LRT",
      elim = buildmer::LRTalpha(0.20),
      quiet = FALSE,
      ddf = "Wald"
    )
    
    bm_res <- run_buildmer_protected(
      buildmer::buildglmmTMB,
      formula = f_zcp, data = data,
      family = binomial(link = "logit"),
      buildmerControl = bm_ctrl,
      timeout_sec = 1800
    )
    
    diag_log$step3_method <- "buildglmmTMB_LRT"
    
  } else {
    # LMM path via buildmer.
    progress_log("[Step 3] Engine: buildmer (lme4-based LRT elimination).", indent = 2)
    bm_ctrl <- buildmer::buildmerControl(
      include = fixed_include,
      direction = c("order", "backward"),
      crit = "LRT",
      elim = buildmer::LRTalpha(0.20),
      quiet = FALSE,
      args = list(control = custom_control_lmer)
    )
    
    bm_res <- run_buildmer_protected(
      buildmer::buildmer,
      formula = f_zcp, data = data,
      buildmerControl = bm_ctrl,
      timeout_sec = 1800
    )
    
    diag_log$step3_method <- "buildmer_LRT"
  }
  
  # Extract reduced model from buildmer result, with fallback to ZCP on
  # timeout/error.
  if (is.null(bm_res)) {
    progress_log("[Step 3] buildmer failed or timed out; retaining ZCP model.",
                 indent = 2)
    m_reduced <- m_zcp
    diag_log$step3_fallback <- "ZCP_after_buildmer_failure"
  } else {
    m_reduced <- tryCatch({
      bm_res@model
    }, error = function(e) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[WARN] Could not extract @model: %s; retaining ZCP.",
                           conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
      m_zcp
    })
    diag_log$step3_fallback <- NA_character_
  }
  
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 3] elapsed: %s", format_elapsed(t_step3)), indent = 2)
  
  # Sanity check: ensure we still have a mixed model.
  if (!inherits(m_reduced, c("merMod", "glmmTMB"))) {
    progress_log("[WARN] Reduced model lost all random effects; refitting with (1 | participant_id).",
                 indent = 2)
    reduced_fixed_str_recovered <- paste(deparse(formula(m_reduced)), collapse = " ")
    f_recover <- as.formula(paste(reduced_fixed_str_recovered, "+ (1 | participant_id)"))
    m_reduced <- fit_func(f_recover, data, REML_flag = FALSE)
  }
  
  diag_log$step3_final_formula <- paste(deparse(formula(m_reduced)), collapse = " ")
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 3] Reduced formula: %s",
                       stringr::str_squish(diag_log$step3_final_formula)),
               indent = 2)
  
  # ---- STEP 4: Test correlation parameters on surviving slopes ----
  progress_log("[Step 4] Testing correlation parameters on surviving slopes...",
               indent = 1)
  t_step4 <- Sys.time()
  
  reduced_fixed <- nobars(formula(m_reduced))
  reduced_fixed_str <- paste(deparse(reduced_fixed), collapse = " ")
  
  m_final <- add_correlations_step4(m_reduced, reduced_fixed_str, data,
                                    model_family = model_family,
                                    alpha_lrt = 0.20)
  diag_log$step4_status <- attr(m_final, "step4_selected") %||% "ZCP_kept"
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 4] elapsed: %s. Selected: %s.",
                       format_elapsed(t_step4), diag_log$step4_status),
               indent = 2)
  
  # ---- STEP 5: rePCA diagnostic ----
  diag_log$step5_pca <- extract_repca_summary(m_final)
  step5_eff <- count_effective_dims(diag_log$step5_pca)
  step5_nom <- nrow(diag_log$step5_pca)
  progress_log(sprintf("[Step 5] Final model dimensionality: %s effective / %s nominal.",
                       if (is.na(step5_eff)) "NA" else as.character(step5_eff),
                       if (is.na(step5_nom)) "NA" else as.character(step5_nom)),
               indent = 1)
  
  # ---- Defensive REML guard for LMM ----
  # 
  # Several paths through add_correlations_step4 and fit_stage1_bates can
  # return an LMM in ML state (REML=FALSE), notably when buildmer's @model
  # slot is preserved verbatim or when ZCP/random-intercept fallbacks fire.
  # lmerTest::anova(ddf="Satterthwaite") expects REML by default and may
  # silently degrade or error on ML-fitted models, triggering the Wald
  # fallback in run_behavior_analysis. We refit REML here unconditionally
  # for LMM (Gaussian) so the downstream Satterthwaite call has a clean
  # input. GLMM models are returned as-is because REML is irrelevant for
  # binomial likelihoods in glmmTMB.
  if (model_family == "gaussian" && inherits(m_final, "merMod")) {
    is_reml <- tryCatch(lme4::isREML(m_final), error = function(e) FALSE)
    if (!isTRUE(is_reml)) {
      progress_log("[Final] Refitting LMM with REML=TRUE for Satterthwaite compatibility.",
                   indent = 1)
      m_final_reml <- tryCatch(
        update(m_final, REML = TRUE, control = custom_control_lmer),
        error = function(e) {
          progress_log(sprintf("[Final] REML refit failed: %s; retaining ML fit.",
                               conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
          NULL
        }
      )
      if (!is.null(m_final_reml)) {
        # Preserve attributes set during Step 4.
        existing_attrs <- attributes(m_final)[c("step4_selected",
                                                "step4_lrt_table")]
        for (an in names(existing_attrs)) {
          if (!is.null(existing_attrs[[an]])) {
            attr(m_final_reml, an) <- existing_attrs[[an]]
          }
        }
        m_final <- m_final_reml
      }
    }
  }
  
  # ---- Defensive lmerTest class upgrade for LMM ----
  #
  # CRITICAL for Satterthwaite/KR p-values. When fit via lme4::lmer() (rather
  # than lmerTest::lmer()), the resulting object has class "lmerMod" only.
  # Calling anova(model, ddf="Satterthwaite") on a bare lmerMod does NOT
  # dispatch to lmerTest's S4 method; instead lme4's base anova() handles it,
  # silently ignoring the ddf argument and returning a table with F values
  # but NO Pr(>F) and NO NumDF/DenDF columns. The downstream cascade then
  # detects "no Pr column" and falls through to Wald.
  #
  # The fix is to upgrade the class to "lmerModLmerTest" via
  # lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(). This is a free operation (no refitting);
  # it merely registers the model with lmerTest's df-computation machinery.
  # 
  # Why this is needed only for some analyses: buildmer internally fits via
  # lmerTest::lmer(), so its @model output may already be lmerModLmerTest.
  # But our add_correlations_step4 refits via lme4::lmer() in many paths,
  # losing the lmerTest class. Result: some analyses go through this gap,
  # others don't, which is exactly the inconsistency observed in v2.0.
  if (model_family == "gaussian" && inherits(m_final, "merMod") &&
      !inherits(m_final, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
    m_final_lt <- tryCatch(
      lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(m_final),
      error = function(e) {
        progress_log(sprintf("[Final] lmerTest class upgrade failed: %s",
                             conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
        NULL
      }
    )
    if (!is.null(m_final_lt)) {
      # Preserve attributes through the class upgrade.
      existing_attrs <- attributes(m_final)[c("step4_selected",
                                              "step4_lrt_table")]
      for (an in names(existing_attrs)) {
        if (!is.null(existing_attrs[[an]])) {
          attr(m_final_lt, an) <- existing_attrs[[an]]
        }
      }
      m_final <- m_final_lt
      progress_log("[Final] LMM upgraded to lmerModLmerTest for Satt/KR dispatch.",
                   indent = 1)
    }
  }
  
  attr(m_final, "bates_diag") <- diag_log
  m_final
}
```


``` {r run-and-report}
# ==============================================================================
# 5. Stage 1 Runner: fit, decompose, report for one analysis.
# ==============================================================================
run_behavior_analysis <- function(data, analysis_name, outcome_var, fixed_terms,
                                  include_terms, model_family, out_dir, exp_version,
                                  posthoc_factors = NULL) {
  
  if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  
  progress_log(sprintf(">>> Analysis: %s [%s] (N_subj = %d, N_trial = %d)",
                       analysis_name, exp_version,
                       dplyr::n_distinct(data$participant_id), nrow(data)))
  
  # ---- Fit Stage 1 model via Bates 5-step ----
  FINAL_MODEL <- fit_stage1_bates(data, outcome_var, fixed_terms,
                                  include_terms, model_family)
  diag_log <- attr(FINAL_MODEL, "bates_diag")
  
  formula_str <- paste(deparse(formula(FINAL_MODEL)), collapse = " ")
  progress_log(sprintf("[Final model] %s", stringr::str_squish(formula_str)),
               indent = 1)
  
  # ---- Type III ANOVA: family-aware strategy. ----
  # 
  # GLMM (binomial, glmmTMB): Wald chi-square is the only viable test.
  #   Satterthwaite df is undefined for non-Gaussian likelihoods (the
  #   approximation requires a residual variance term that does not exist
  #   in the binomial likelihood; variance is determined by the mean
  #   structure as Var(y) = p(1-p)).
  # 
  # LMM (Gaussian, lme4): cascading method preference:
  #   (1) Satterthwaite F  - lmerTest::anova; preferred (Luke 2017).
  #   (2) Kenward-Roger F  - pbkrtest backend; conservative fallback.
  #       KR uses a different numerical path than Satterthwaite, so
  #       it can succeed when Satterthwaite hits Hessian inversion
  #       failure modes on certain ill-conditioned random structures.
  #   (3) Wald chi-square  - car::Anova; last resort, asymptotic only.
  #       Anti-conservative for finite N; flagged in REPRODUCIBILITY.
  # The cascade tries each in turn; the first to return a valid p-value
  # column wins. Method actually used is logged transparently.
  progress_log("[ANOVA] Computing Type III tests...", indent = 1)
  t_anova <- Sys.time()
  
  if (model_family == "binomial") {
    anova_res <- car::Anova(FINAL_MODEL, type = 3, test.statistic = "Chisq")
    diag_log$anova_method <- "Wald_chi_square_GLMM"
  } else {
    # LMM cascade: Satterthwaite -> Kenward-Roger -> Wald.
    # Defensive: ensure class includes lmerModLmerTest. fit_stage1_bates
    # already upgrades, but if FINAL_MODEL was supplied through some other
    # path (e.g. user reloads from RDS and calls run_behavior_analysis
    # directly), this protects against bare lmerMod silently bypassing
    # lmerTest's anova dispatch.
    if (inherits(FINAL_MODEL, "merMod") &&
        !inherits(FINAL_MODEL, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
      FINAL_MODEL_lt <- tryCatch(
        lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(FINAL_MODEL),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
      if (!is.null(FINAL_MODEL_lt)) FINAL_MODEL <- FINAL_MODEL_lt
    }
    
    anova_res <- NULL
    method_used <- NA_character_
    
    # Attempt 1: Satterthwaite.
    anova_res <- tryCatch({
      res <- suppressWarnings(anova(FINAL_MODEL, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite"))
      if (any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
        method_used <- "Satterthwaite_F"
        res
      } else {
        progress_log("[ANOVA] Satterthwaite returned no p-value column; trying Kenward-Roger.",
                     indent = 2)
        NULL
      }
    }, error = function(e) {
      progress_log(sprintf("[ANOVA] Satterthwaite errored (%s); trying Kenward-Roger.",
                           conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
      NULL
    })
    
    # Attempt 2: Kenward-Roger.
    if (is.null(anova_res)) {
      anova_res <- tryCatch({
        res <- suppressWarnings(anova(FINAL_MODEL, type = 3, ddf = "Kenward-Roger"))
        if (any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
          method_used <- "Kenward_Roger_F"
          res
        } else {
          progress_log("[ANOVA] Kenward-Roger returned no p-value column; falling back to Wald.",
                       indent = 2)
          NULL
        }
      }, error = function(e) {
        progress_log(sprintf("[ANOVA] Kenward-Roger errored (%s); falling back to Wald.",
                             conditionMessage(e)), indent = 2)
        NULL
      })
    }
    
    # Attempt 3: Wald.
    if (is.null(anova_res)) {
      anova_res <- car::Anova(FINAL_MODEL, type = 3, test.statistic = "Chisq")
      method_used <- "Wald_chi_square"
    }
    
    diag_log$anova_method <- method_used
  }
  
  progress_log(sprintf("[ANOVA] Method: %s. Elapsed: %s.",
                       diag_log$anova_method, format_elapsed(t_anova)),
               indent = 2)
  
  anova_apa <- format_anova_apa(anova_res, FINAL_MODEL)
  print(anova_apa %>% dplyr::select(Effect, APA_Report, Sig))
  
  # ---- Post-hoc decomposition ----
  # Determine the primary interaction term to gate post-hoc on.
  # For GLMM_rejection and LMM_RT_main: emotion:offer_type
  # For LMM_RT_unfair                  : emotion:reaction
  progress_log("[Post-hoc] Extracting marginal means and contrasts...", indent = 1)
  
  target_2way <- if ("emotion:offer_type" %in% rownames(anova_res)) {
    "emotion:offer_type"
  } else if ("emotion:reaction" %in% rownames(anova_res)) {
    "emotion:reaction"
  } else NA_character_
  
  p_int_2way <- NA_real_
  if (!is.na(target_2way) && target_2way %in% rownames(anova_res)) {
    for (pcol in c("Pr(>F)", "Pr(>Chisq)")) {
      if (pcol %in% colnames(anova_res)) {
        val <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(anova_res[target_2way, pcol]))
        if (length(val) == 1 && !is.na(val)) {
          p_int_2way <- val; break
        }
      }
    }
  }
  if (is.na(p_int_2way)) p_int_2way <- 1.0
  
  list_of_tables <- list(
    "ANOVA_Main" = anova_apa,
    "Model_Formula" = data.frame(Formula = formula_str),
    "Model_Coefficients" = format_coefs(FINAL_MODEL)
  )
  
  # Determine post-hoc factor pair from analysis_name.
  # GLMM_rejection / LMM_RT_main : factor pair (offer_type, emotion)
  # LMM_RT_unfair                : factor pair (reaction, emotion)
  if (is.null(posthoc_factors)) {
    if (analysis_name == "LMM_RT_unfair") {
      posthoc_factors <- list(within = "reaction", between = "emotion")
    } else {
      posthoc_factors <- list(within = "offer_type", between = "emotion")
    }
  }
  f_within <- posthoc_factors$within
  f_between <- posthoc_factors$between
  
  # Scale hint for format_posthoc_apa: drives OR (GLMM) vs percent-change (logRT)
  # column appendage on contrast tables.
  scale_hint <- dplyr::case_when(
    model_family == "binomial" ~ "logit",
    outcome_var == "logRT"     ~ "logRT",
    TRUE                        ~ "raw"
  )
  
  # Helper closure: emmeans -> contrast pairs with 95% CI included.
  # summary(infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)) returns BOTH confidence intervals AND
  # significance tests in one object, so format_posthoc_apa downstream finds
  # lower.CL / upper.CL columns rather than reconstructing them from SE.
  pairs_with_ci <- function(emm, adjust = "fdr") {
    pp <- pairs(emm, adjust = adjust)
    summary(pp, infer = c(TRUE, TRUE))
  }
  
  # Confirmatory branch: omnibus interaction p < confirmatory_alpha (= 0.05).
  # Marginal branch: confirmatory_alpha <= p < marginal_threshold (= 0.10).
  # Marginal contrasts are computed but routed to Supplementary, not main.
  posthoc_status <- dplyr::case_when(
    p_int_2way < confirmatory_alpha             ~ "Confirmatory",
    p_int_2way < marginal_threshold             ~ "Exploratory_Marginal",
    TRUE                                         ~ "Not_triggered"
  )
  
  # Container for marginal contrasts (routed to Supplementary).
  list_of_supp_tables <- list()
  
  if (posthoc_status %in% c("Confirmatory", "Exploratory_Marginal")) {
    target_list <- if (posthoc_status == "Confirmatory") "list_of_tables" else "list_of_supp_tables"
    progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc] Interaction p = %.4f -> %s. Routing simple effects to %s.",
                         p_int_2way, posthoc_status,
                         ifelse(target_list == "list_of_tables", "main", "Supplementary")),
                 indent = 1)
    
    progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc 1/3] %s | %s (FDR)...", f_within, f_between),
                 indent = 2)
    t_ph <- Sys.time()
    f1 <- as.formula(sprintf("~ %s | %s", f_within, f_between))
    so_em <- format_posthoc_apa(
      pairs_with_ci(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, f1), adjust = "fdr"),
      scale_hint = scale_hint
    )
    progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc 1/3] done (%s).", format_elapsed(t_ph)), indent = 3)
    so_em$Status <- posthoc_status
    
    progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc 2/3] %s | %s (FDR)...", f_between, f_within),
                 indent = 2)
    t_ph <- Sys.time()
    f2 <- as.formula(sprintf("~ %s | %s", f_between, f_within))
    se_off <- format_posthoc_apa(
      pairs_with_ci(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, f2), adjust = "fdr"),
      scale_hint = scale_hint
    )
    progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc 2/3] done (%s).", format_elapsed(t_ph)), indent = 3)
    se_off$Status <- posthoc_status
    
    progress_log("[Post-hoc 3/3] interaction contrasts (FDR)...", indent = 2)
    t_ph <- Sys.time()
    f3 <- as.formula(sprintf("~ %s * %s", f_between, f_within))
    int_contr <- format_posthoc_apa(
      summary(contrast(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL, f3),
                       interaction = "pairwise", adjust = "fdr"),
              infer = c(TRUE, TRUE)),
      scale_hint = scale_hint
    )
    progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc 3/3] done (%s).", format_elapsed(t_ph)), indent = 3)
    int_contr$Status <- posthoc_status
    
    if (posthoc_status == "Confirmatory") {
      list_of_tables[[sprintf("Simple_%s_by_%s", f_within, f_between)]] <- so_em
      list_of_tables[[sprintf("Simple_%s_by_%s", f_between, f_within)]] <- se_off
      list_of_tables[["Interaction_Contrasts"]] <- int_contr
    } else {
      list_of_supp_tables[[sprintf("MARGINAL_Simple_%s_by_%s", f_within, f_between)]] <- so_em
      list_of_supp_tables[[sprintf("MARGINAL_Simple_%s_by_%s", f_between, f_within)]] <- se_off
      list_of_supp_tables[["MARGINAL_Interaction_Contrasts"]] <- int_contr
    }
    
  } else {
    progress_log(sprintf("[Post-hoc] Interaction p = %.4f -> Reporting main effects only.",
                         p_int_2way), indent = 1)
  }
  
  # Always extract main effects (always in main tables).
  progress_log(sprintf("[Main effect] %s pairwise (FDR)...", f_between), indent = 2)
  t_me <- Sys.time()
  list_of_tables[[sprintf("Main_Effect_%s", f_between)]] <- format_posthoc_apa(
    pairs_with_ci(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL,
                                   as.formula(sprintf("~ %s", f_between))),
                  adjust = "fdr"),
    scale_hint = scale_hint
  )
  progress_log(sprintf("[Main effect %s] done (%s).", f_between, format_elapsed(t_me)),
               indent = 3)
  
  progress_log(sprintf("[Main effect] %s pairwise (Tukey)...", f_within), indent = 2)
  t_me <- Sys.time()
  list_of_tables[[sprintf("Main_Effect_%s", f_within)]] <- format_posthoc_apa(
    pairs_with_ci(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL,
                                   as.formula(sprintf("~ %s", f_within))),
                  adjust = "tukey"),
    scale_hint = scale_hint
  )
  progress_log(sprintf("[Main effect %s] done (%s).", f_within, format_elapsed(t_me)),
               indent = 3)
  
  progress_log("[Descriptive] estimated marginal means...", indent = 2)
  t_me <- Sys.time()
  list_of_tables[["Descriptive_Means"]] <- beautify_labels(kill_scipen(
    as.data.frame(emmeans::emmeans(FINAL_MODEL,
                                   as.formula(sprintf("~ %s * %s", f_within, f_between))))
  ))
  progress_log(sprintf("[Descriptive] done (%s).", format_elapsed(t_me)), indent = 3)
  
  # Cell-level raw descriptives (Table 1 candidate). Computed from data, not
  # from emmeans -- gives the reader N, raw rejection rate, raw RT distribution.
  progress_log("[Descriptive] cell-level raw statistics...", indent = 2)
  list_of_tables[["Cell_Descriptives"]] <- format_descriptives_table(
    data, group_vars = c(f_between, f_within)
  )
  
  # ---- Reporting Layer ----
  # 1. REPRODUCIBILITY metadata.
  sink(file.path(out_dir, "REPRODUCIBILITY.txt"))
  cat("# Reproducibility log for behavioral analysis:", analysis_name, "\n")
  cat("# Generated:", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "\n\n")
  cat("## Final formula:\n")
  cat(formula_str, "\n\n")
  cat("## Software versions:\n")
  cat("R:        ", R.version.string, "\n")
  cat("lme4:     ", as.character(packageVersion("lme4")), "\n")
  cat("lmerTest: ", as.character(packageVersion("lmerTest")), "\n")
  cat("glmmTMB:  ", as.character(packageVersion("glmmTMB")), "\n")
  cat("buildmer: ", as.character(packageVersion("buildmer")), "\n")
  cat("emmeans:  ", as.character(packageVersion("emmeans")), "\n\n")
  cat("## Model family:    ", model_family, "\n")
  cat("## Engine:          ", if (inherits(FINAL_MODEL, "glmmTMB")) "glmmTMB"
                              else if (inherits(FINAL_MODEL, "merMod")) "lme4"
                              else class(FINAL_MODEL)[1], "\n")
  cat("## Outcome variable:", outcome_var, "\n")
  cat("## Convergence:\n")
  
  # Engine-agnostic singularity reporting.
  is_sing_final <- if (inherits(FINAL_MODEL, "glmmTMB")) {
    vc <- VarCorr(FINAL_MODEL)$cond
    if (is.null(vc)) FALSE
    else any(unlist(lapply(vc, function(x) diag(as.matrix(x)))) < 1e-6)
  } else {
    lme4::isSingular(FINAL_MODEL, tol = 1e-4)
  }
  cat("Singular fit:", is_sing_final, "\n")
  cat("Observations:", nobs(FINAL_MODEL), "\n")
  
  # Engine-agnostic ngrps.
  ngrps_final <- if (inherits(FINAL_MODEL, "glmmTMB")) {
    summary(FINAL_MODEL)$ngrps$cond["participant_id"]
  } else {
    lme4::ngrps(FINAL_MODEL)["participant_id"]
  }
  cat("Subjects:    ", ngrps_final, "\n\n")
  cat("## Bates 5-step diagnostic log:\n")
  
  # Step 3 method: both LMM and GLMM use buildmer (different engines).
  step3_method_str <- diag_log$step3_method %||% "buildmer_LRT"
  if (step3_method_str == "buildglmmTMB_LRT") {
    cat("Step 3 method:               buildmer::buildglmmTMB() LRT (GLMM)\n")
  } else {
    cat("Step 3 method:               buildmer::buildmer() LRT (LMM)\n")
  }
  cat("Term ordering criterion:     LRT (default)\n")
  cat("Term elimination criterion:  LRTalpha(0.20) (Matuschek et al., 2017)\n")
  cat("Engineering protections:     lmerTest detached during buildmer call;\n")
  cat("                             withTimeout=1800s; ZCP fallback on failure.\n")
  if (!is.na(diag_log$step3_fallback %||% NA_character_)) {
    cat("Step 3 fallback triggered:  ", diag_log$step3_fallback, "\n")
  }
  
  cat("Step 1 (Maximal):           ", diag_log$step1_status, "\n")
  if (!is.null(diag_log$step1_pca)) {
    cat("  Step 1 effective/nominal: ",
        count_effective_dims(diag_log$step1_pca), "/",
        nrow(diag_log$step1_pca), "\n")
  }
  cat("Step 2 (ZCP):               ", diag_log$step2_status, "\n")
  cat("Step 3 final formula:       ", diag_log$step3_final_formula %||% "n/a", "\n")
  cat("Step 4 (correlations):      ", diag_log$step4_status, "\n")
  cat("Step 5 (final dims):        ",
      count_effective_dims(diag_log$step5_pca), "/",
      nrow(diag_log$step5_pca), "\n")
  cat("\n## Inferential method:\n")
  cat("ANOVA test:                 ", diag_log$anova_method %||% "Wald_chi_square", "\n")
  if (identical(diag_log$anova_method, "Wald_chi_square")) {
    cat("Note: Satterthwaite was attempted but failed (no p-value column or\n")
    cat("error). Wald chi-square (car::Anova) used as fallback.\n")
  }
  sink()
  
  # 2. Full model summary.
  sink(file.path(out_dir, "summary_text.txt"))
  print(summary(FINAL_MODEL))
  sink()
  
  # 3. ANOVA table in markdown.
  writeLines(
    knitr::kable(anova_apa, format = "markdown",
                 caption = sprintf("Type III ANOVA (%s), %s.",
                                   diag_log$anova_method %||% "unknown", analysis_name)),
    con = file.path(out_dir, "anova_apa.md")
  )
  
  # 4. R-squared (Nakagawa & Schielzeth, 2013).
  r2_obj <- tryCatch(performance::r2(FINAL_MODEL), error = function(e) NULL)
  if (!is.null(r2_obj)) {
    r2_df <- data.frame(
      R2_marginal    = r2_obj$R2_marginal %||% NA_real_,
      R2_conditional = r2_obj$R2_conditional %||% NA_real_
    )
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(kill_scipen(r2_df), format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("Nakagawa & Schielzeth R\u00B2, %s.", analysis_name)),
      con = file.path(out_dir, "r2.md")
    )
  }
  
  # 5. Post-hoc tables.
  for (nm in names(list_of_tables)) {
    safe_nm <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", nm)
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(list_of_tables[[nm]], format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("%s -- %s", analysis_name, nm)),
      con = file.path(out_dir, sprintf("posthoc_%s.md", safe_nm))
    )
  }
  
  # 6. Step 4 LRT (when applicable).
  step4_lrt <- attr(FINAL_MODEL, "step4_lrt_table")
  if (!is.null(step4_lrt) && nrow(step4_lrt) > 0) {
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(kill_scipen(step4_lrt), format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("Step 4 candidate-correlation LRT, %s.", analysis_name)),
      con = file.path(out_dir, "step4_correlation_lrt.md")
    )
  }
  
  # 7. Bates rePCA in markdown.
  if (!is.null(diag_log$step5_pca) && !all(is.na(diag_log$step5_pca$component))) {
    writeLines(
      knitr::kable(kill_scipen(diag_log$step5_pca), format = "markdown",
                   caption = sprintf("Final-model rePCA dimensionality, %s.", analysis_name)),
      con = file.path(out_dir, "step5_rePCA.md")
    )
  }
  
  # 7b. Supplementary tables: marginal contrasts (0.05 <= p < 0.10) go here,
  # not in the main analysis directory. This separates confirmatory from
  # exploratory inference physically, not just by Status column tag.
  if (length(list_of_supp_tables) > 0) {
    supp_subdir <- file.path(out_suppl,
                             sprintf("%s_marginal_contrasts", analysis_name))
    if (!dir.exists(supp_subdir)) dir.create(supp_subdir, recursive = TRUE)
    for (nm in names(list_of_supp_tables)) {
      safe_nm <- gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", nm)
      writeLines(
        knitr::kable(list_of_supp_tables[[nm]], format = "markdown",
                     caption = sprintf("%s -- %s (omnibus interaction p in [0.05, 0.10); EXPLORATORY ONLY)",
                                       analysis_name, nm)),
        con = file.path(supp_subdir, sprintf("%s.md", safe_nm))
      )
    }
    progress_log(sprintf("[Supplementary] %d marginal table(s) written to %s",
                         length(list_of_supp_tables),
                         file.path("Supplementary",
                                   sprintf("%s_marginal_contrasts", analysis_name))),
                 indent = 1)
  }
  
  # 7c. Save the fitted model object for downstream re-extraction.
  # Naming convention: final_model_<analysis_name>.rds for cross-directory
  # identifiability when manually inspecting results.
  rds_path <- file.path(out_dir, sprintf("final_model_%s.rds", analysis_name))
  saveRDS(FINAL_MODEL, file = rds_path)
  progress_log(sprintf("[Save] Model object: %s", basename(rds_path)), indent = 1)
  
  # 8. Excel export (legacy compatibility).
  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
  for (sheet_name in names(list_of_tables)) {
    safe_sheet <- substr(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9_]", "_", sheet_name), 1, 31)
    openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, safe_sheet)
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, safe_sheet, list_of_tables[[sheet_name]])
    openxlsx::addStyle(wb, safe_sheet,
      openxlsx::createStyle(textDecoration = "bold", border = "Bottom"),
      rows = 1, cols = 1:ncol(list_of_tables[[sheet_name]]))
  }
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb,
    file.path(out_dir, sprintf("STATS_%s_%s.xlsx", exp_version, analysis_name)),
    overwrite = TRUE)
  
  # ---- Visualization removed in v1.6.
  # 
  # Rationale: Publication-quality figures are generated by the downstream
  # Python pipeline (Visualization_Behavior.py), which produces rain-cloud,
  # forest, and faceted interaction plots with consistent typography across
  # all analyses. R-side ggplot/sjPlot PDFs were redundant sanity-check
  # output. To verify model fit, inspect emm_apa.md and posthoc_*.md files
  # in the analysis output directory, or run summary(FINAL_MODEL) interactively.

  progress_log(">>> Analysis complete.", indent = 1)
  invisible(FINAL_MODEL)
}

# ==============================================================================
# Multi-analysis side-by-side report (for manuscript).
# Mirrors EEG v12 logic with HTML + markdown fallback.
# ==============================================================================
report_behavior_multi <- function(model_list, exp_version, out_dir) {
  if (length(model_list) == 0) return(invisible(NULL))
  
  out_html <- file.path(out_dir, sprintf("Behavior_AllAnalyses_%s.html", exp_version))
  out_md   <- file.path(out_dir, sprintf("Behavior_AllAnalyses_%s.md", exp_version))
  
  # ---- HTML output via sjPlot::tab_model ----
  tab_model_succeeded <- FALSE
  tryCatch({
    sjPlot::tab_model(
      model_list,
      show.se = TRUE, show.stat = TRUE, show.ci = FALSE,
      string.se = "SE", string.stat = "stat", string.p = "p-value",
      show.re.var = TRUE, show.obs = TRUE, show.icc = FALSE,
      show.r2 = TRUE, show.loglik = TRUE, show.dev = TRUE,
      emph.p = TRUE, p.style = "numeric_stars",
      file = out_html,
      dv.labels = names(model_list)
    )
    if (file.exists(out_html) && file.size(out_html) > 0) {
      cat(sprintf("[Multi-analysis HTML] %s\n", basename(out_html)))
      tab_model_succeeded <- TRUE
    } else {
      cat(sprintf("[WARN] tab_model returned without error but no file written: %s\n",
                  out_html))
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("[WARN] tab_model failed: %s\n", conditionMessage(e)))
  })
  
  # ---- Markdown fallback ----
  tryCatch({
    rows <- list()
    methods_log <- character(0)
    for (a_name in names(model_list)) {
      mdl <- model_list[[a_name]]
      
      # GLMM (glmmTMB or glmerMod): Wald only.
      # LMM (merMod): Satterthwaite -> Kenward-Roger -> Wald cascade,
      # mirroring the cascade in run_behavior_analysis.
      anova_obj <- NULL
      method_used <- NA_character_
      
      if (inherits(mdl, c("glmerMod", "glmmTMB"))) {
        anova_obj <- tryCatch(
          car::Anova(mdl, type = 3, test.statistic = "Chisq"),
          error = function(e) NULL
        )
        method_used <- "Wald chi-square (GLMM)"
      } else {
        # LMM path. Defensive: ensure class includes lmerModLmerTest so
        # anova() dispatches to lmerTest's Satterthwaite/KR methods rather
        # than lme4's base anova (which silently ignores the ddf argument
        # and returns no p-value column). See fit_stage1_bates for the
        # primary upgrade location; this is a redundant safeguard for the
        # case where models are loaded from disk and passed directly here.
        if (!inherits(mdl, "lmerModLmerTest")) {
          mdl_upgraded <- tryCatch(
            lmerTest::as_lmerModLmerTest(mdl),
            error = function(e) NULL
          )
          if (!is.null(mdl_upgraded)) mdl <- mdl_upgraded
        }
        
        # Attempt 1: Satterthwaite.
        anova_obj <- tryCatch({
          res <- suppressWarnings(anova(mdl, type = 3, ddf = "Satterthwaite"))
          if (any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
            method_used <- "Satterthwaite F"
            res
          } else {
            NULL
          }
        }, error = function(e) NULL)
        
        # Attempt 2: Kenward-Roger.
        if (is.null(anova_obj)) {
          anova_obj <- tryCatch({
            res <- suppressWarnings(anova(mdl, type = 3, ddf = "Kenward-Roger"))
            if (any(grepl("^Pr", colnames(res)))) {
              method_used <- "Kenward-Roger F"
              res
            } else {
              NULL
            }
          }, error = function(e) NULL)
        }
        
        # Attempt 3: Wald.
        if (is.null(anova_obj)) {
          anova_obj <- tryCatch(
            car::Anova(mdl, type = 3, test.statistic = "Chisq"),
            error = function(e) NULL
          )
          if (!is.null(anova_obj)) {
            method_used <- "Wald chi-square (LMM fallback)"
          }
        }
      }
      
      if (is.null(anova_obj)) next
      
      methods_log <- c(methods_log, sprintf("%s: %s", a_name, method_used))
      apa <- format_anova_apa(anova_obj, mdl)
      apa$Analysis <- a_name
      apa$Method <- method_used
      rows[[a_name]] <- apa[, c("Analysis", "Effect", "APA_Report", "Sig", "Method")]
    }
    
    if (length(rows) > 0) {
      combined <- do.call(rbind, rows)
      writeLines(
        c(sprintf("# Behavioral Analysis Summary, %s", exp_version),
          sprintf("Generated: %s", format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")),
          "",
          "Type III ANOVA tests. LMM analyses use a Satterthwaite -> ",
          "Kenward-Roger -> Wald cascade (lmerTest, pbkrtest, car). GLMM ",
          "analyses use Wald chi-square (car::Anova) as the only valid ",
          "method (Satterthwaite is undefined for non-Gaussian likelihoods). ",
          "The actual method used per analysis is shown in the Method column.",
          "",
          "## Methods used per analysis:",
          paste0("- ", methods_log),
          "",
          knitr::kable(combined, format = "markdown",
                       caption = sprintf("Behavioral fixed-effect tests across %d analyses.",
                                         length(rows)))),
        con = out_md
      )
      cat(sprintf("[Multi-analysis Markdown] %s\n", basename(out_md)))
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("[WARN] Markdown multi-analysis summary failed: %s\n",
                conditionMessage(e)))
  })
  
  invisible(list(html_ok = tab_model_succeeded, html_path = out_html, md_path = out_md))
}
```

``` {r execution}
# ==============================================================================
# 6. Execution Phase
# ==============================================================================
path_pipeline <- here("data", paste0("02_Pipeline_Output_", experiment_version))
path_trials <- file.path(path_pipeline, "Method_Regression", "Stimulus_Locked", "trials.csv")

if (!file.exists(path_trials)) {
  stop(sprintf("Trial file not found: %s\nVerify upstream preprocessing.", path_trials))
}

cat("--- Loading and preparing behavioral data ---\n")
df_clean <- load_and_prep_behavior(path_trials)

# ---- Subset for unfair-only analysis ----
df_unfair <- df_clean %>% dplyr::filter(offer_type == "unfair")
cat(sprintf("\n[Subset] Unfair-only data: %d trials, %d subjects\n",
            nrow(df_unfair), dplyr::n_distinct(df_unfair$participant_id)))

# Check uniqueness for both subsets.
check_uniqueness(df_clean, "df_clean")
check_uniqueness(df_unfair, "df_unfair")

# ---- Run all configured analyses ----
behavior_models <- list()
total_analyses <- length(analyses_to_run)
pipeline_t0 <- Sys.time()

for (a_idx in seq_along(analyses_to_run)) {
  a_name <- analyses_to_run[a_idx]
  
  progress_log(sprintf(">>> [%d/%d] Analysis: %s (cumulative pipeline time: %s)",
                       a_idx, total_analyses, a_name,
                       format_elapsed(pipeline_t0)))
  
  # Configure each analysis based on its name.
  config <- switch(a_name,
    "GLMM_rejection" = list(
      data = df_clean,
      outcome = "reject_binary",
      fixed_terms = "(emotion + offer_type)^2",
      include = c("emotion", "offer_type", "emotion:offer_type"),
      family = "binomial",
      out = out_glmm,
      posthoc = list(within = "offer_type", between = "emotion")
    ),
    "LMM_RT_main" = list(
      data = df_clean,
      outcome = "logRT",
      # All trials, emotion x offer_type only. reaction is NOT included as
      # covariate -- it is a downstream outcome of the manipulations and
      # conditioning on it would induce collider bias (Rohrer, 2018, AMPPS).
      # The accept-vs-reject decision dynamics on unfair offers are addressed
      # separately via LMM_RT_unfair below.
      fixed_terms = "(emotion + offer_type)^2",
      include = c("emotion", "offer_type", "emotion:offer_type"),
      family = "gaussian",
      out = out_lmm_main,
      posthoc = list(within = "offer_type", between = "emotion")
    ),
    "LMM_RT_unfair" = list(
      data = df_unfair,
      outcome = "logRT",
      # Unfair-only: tests emotion x reaction (HDDM-parallel: how emotion
      # modulates the accept-vs-reject decision time on unfair offers).
      fixed_terms = "(emotion + reaction)^2",
      include = c("emotion", "reaction", "emotion:reaction"),
      family = "gaussian",
      out = out_lmm_unfair,
      posthoc = list(within = "reaction", between = "emotion")
    ),
    NULL  # Unknown analysis name -> skip
  )
  
  if (is.null(config)) {
    progress_log(sprintf("[SKIP] Unknown analysis: %s", a_name))
    next
  }
  
  fit <- run_behavior_analysis(
    data = config$data,
    analysis_name = a_name,
    outcome_var = config$outcome,
    fixed_terms = config$fixed_terms,
    include_terms = config$include,
    model_family = config$family,
    out_dir = config$out,
    exp_version = experiment_version,
    posthoc_factors = config$posthoc
  )
  
  if (!is.null(fit)) {
    behavior_models[[a_name]] <- fit
  }
  progress_log(sprintf(">>> [%d/%d] %s complete.", a_idx, total_analyses, a_name))
}

# ---- Multi-analysis summary table ----
report_behavior_multi(behavior_models, experiment_version, out_tables)

cat(sprintf("\n[Behavioral pipeline complete] Fitted %d/%d analyses.\n",
            length(behavior_models), total_analyses))
```

``` {r methods-paragraph}
# ==============================================================================
# 7. Methods paragraph (manuscript-ready text)
# 
# Outputs a markdown file with a methods paragraph that can be pasted directly
# into the manuscript. Contains: contrast coding, random-structure selection
# protocol, inferential strategy, post-hoc strategy, effect-size reporting,
# and the design-level rationale for not modeling stimulus identity.
# ==============================================================================
methods_paragraph <- sprintf('# Methods Paragraph (Behavioral Analyses, %s)

Generated: %s

## Statistical Analysis

Behavioral data were analyzed using mixed-effects models in R (version %s)
with the lme4 (%s) and lmerTest (%s) packages, with binomial models fitted
via glmmTMB (%s). Categorical predictors used sum-to-zero contrasts (R option
contr.sum) to support valid Type III tests in the presence of interactions
(Schad, Vasishth, Hohenstein, & Kliegl, 2020). Trials were excluded if the
participant did not respond (reaction = 0), if the response time fell outside
%d-%d ms, or if the offer was the medium-fairness filler (Offers_Other = 7).

### Models

We fitted three models on Experiment %s data:

1. **Rejection rate (GLMM_rejection):** A binomial mixed-effects model on a
   binary rejection outcome with predictors emotion (5 levels), offer type
   (fair vs unfair), and their interaction.

2. **Response time, main analysis (LMM_RT_main):** A linear mixed-effects
   model on log-transformed response time with predictors emotion, offer
   type, and their interaction. Reaction (accept vs reject) was deliberately
   NOT included as a covariate because it is a downstream outcome of
   emotion x offer_type; conditioning on a downstream variable induces
   collider bias and would distort the total emotion-on-RT effect (Rohrer,
   2018).

3. **Response time, unfair-only (LMM_RT_unfair):** A linear mixed-effects
   model on log-transformed response time restricted to unfair offers, with
   predictors emotion, reaction, and their interaction. This stratum
   parallels the HDDM modeling of accept-vs-reject decision dynamics on
   unfair offers.

### Random-effects structure

Random-effects structures were selected following the parsimonious-Bates
protocol (Bates, Kliegl, Vasishth, & Baayen, 2015; Matuschek, Kliegl,
Vasishth, Baayen, & Bates, 2017). Starting from the design-justified
maximal model (random intercepts and slopes for within-subject factors
emotion and offer type by participant), zero-correlation parameter (ZCP)
models were fitted, then non-supported variance components were removed
via likelihood-ratio tests with elimination alpha = 0.20 (Matuschek et al.,
2017) using the buildmer package. Correlation parameters between surviving
slopes were tested in a final step. Random-effects dimensionality was
diagnosed via rePCA (Bates et al., 2015). Stimulus identity was
counterbalanced across participants via a Latin-square design and was not
modeled as a separate random effect; identity-level idiosyncrasies are thus
controlled at the design level rather than statistically partitioned (cf.
Westfall, Kenny, & Judd, 2014).

### Inferential strategy

For linear mixed models, fixed-effect inference used a Type III F-test with
denominator degrees of freedom approximated via a cascading method
preference: Satterthwaite (Kuznetsova, Brockhoff, & Christensen, 2017;
Luke, 2017) was attempted first; on numerical failure, Kenward-Roger
(Kenward & Roger, 1997; via the pbkrtest backend) was attempted next;
Wald chi-square (car::Anova) was used only as a final fallback. The
method actually used per analysis is reported in supplementary tables.
For the binomial model, Wald chi-square tests were used because the
Satterthwaite and Kenward-Roger approximations are not defined for
non-Gaussian likelihoods (the residual variance term they require does
not exist in binomial-likelihood models, where Var(y) is determined by
the mean structure as p(1-p)). Post-hoc contrasts were computed using
the emmeans package (Lenth, 2024) with asymptotic standard errors and
false-discovery-rate (FDR) correction within each effect family.

### Effect-size reporting

For Gaussian models, partial eta-squared with 95%% confidence intervals are
reported alongside F-tests (effectsize::eta_squared). For the binomial
model, odds ratios with 95%% CIs are reported for fixed-effect contrasts.
For log-RT contrasts, percent RT change is reported as
(exp(b) - 1) x 100. Marginal and conditional R-squared (Nakagawa &
Schielzeth, 2013) are reported for all models.

### Post-hoc gating

Simple-effect decompositions of the omnibus emotion x offer_type (or
emotion x reaction) interaction were performed only when the omnibus
interaction p < %.2f. Effects with %.2f <= p < %.2f were computed but
reported only in supplementary materials, never as confirmatory evidence.

## Sample

%d trials from %d participants entered the GLMM_rejection and LMM_RT_main
analyses; the LMM_RT_unfair stratum included %d trials.

## References (cite as appropriate)

Bates, D., Kliegl, R., Vasishth, S., & Baayen, R. H. (2015).
  Parsimonious mixed models. arXiv:1506.04967.
Halekoh, U., & Hojsgaard, S. (2014). A Kenward-Roger approximation and
  parametric bootstrap methods for tests in linear mixed models -- the R
  package pbkrtest. Journal of Statistical Software, 59(9).
Kenward, M. G., & Roger, J. H. (1997). Small sample inference for fixed
  effects from restricted maximum likelihood. Biometrics, 53, 983-997.
Kuznetsova, A., Brockhoff, P. B., & Christensen, R. H. B. (2017).
  lmerTest package: Tests in linear mixed effects models. Journal of
  Statistical Software, 82(13).
Lenth, R. V. (2024). emmeans: Estimated marginal means.
Luke, S. G. (2017). Evaluating significance in linear mixed-effects models
  in R. Behavior Research Methods, 49, 1494-1502.
Matuschek, H., Kliegl, R., Vasishth, S., Baayen, H., & Bates, D. (2017).
  Balancing Type I error and power in linear mixed models. Journal of
  Memory and Language, 94, 305-315.
Nakagawa, S., & Schielzeth, H. (2013). A general and simple method for
  obtaining R^2 from generalized linear mixed-effects models. Methods in
  Ecology and Evolution, 4, 133-142.
Rohrer, J. M. (2018). Thinking clearly about correlations and causation.
  Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science, 1, 27-42.
Schad, D. J., Vasishth, S., Hohenstein, S., & Kliegl, R. (2020). How to
  capitalize on a priori contrasts in linear (mixed) models. Journal of
  Memory and Language, 110, 104038.
Westfall, J., Kenny, D. A., & Judd, C. M. (2014). Statistical power and
  optimal design in experiments in which samples of participants respond
  to samples of stimuli. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General,
  143, 2020-2045.
',
  experiment_version,
  format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"),
  paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = "."),
  as.character(packageVersion("lme4")),
  as.character(packageVersion("lmerTest")),
  as.character(packageVersion("glmmTMB")),
  rt_lower_ms, rt_upper_ms,
  experiment_version,
  confirmatory_alpha, confirmatory_alpha, marginal_threshold,
  nrow(df_clean), dplyr::n_distinct(df_clean$participant_id),
  nrow(df_unfair)
)

writeLines(methods_paragraph,
           con = file.path(out_tables,
                           sprintf("Methods_paragraph_%s.md", experiment_version)))
cat(sprintf("[Methods] Methods_paragraph_%s.md written to %s\n",
            experiment_version, basename(out_tables)))
```
